answer.value: The functions of the UPSC (Article 320) are: (1) to conduct competitive examinations for recruitment to the posts of Group ‘A’ and ‘B’ of the Union Government; (2) to conduct the Personality Test for direct recruitment; (3) to advise the Government on the guidelines to be followed in promotions and transfers of various posts; (4) to advise the Government on disciplinary actions against the misconduct of officials in Central and State Governments; (5) to advise the Government on any matter as per the instructions of the President of India.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Although both Sugarcane and Tobacco are commercial crops, there is a difference in the geographical factors required for their cultivation. Justify.

answer.value: Sugarcane needs a climate of high temperature and moisture — a temperature of 21° to 26° Celsius and 100–150 cm of annual rainfall — and alluvial and black soil is most suitable for it. Tobacco, on the other hand, is grown mainly on the black soil regions (for example, Nipani in Belagavi district of Karnataka), so the two commercial crops differ in the soil and climatic factors they require.

Karnataka’s Nipani town of Belagavi district is the [tobacco region].". The MQP prints no answer key; answer sourced from the textbook per review_policy_v1 §2-4.

answer_evidence.text: This crop needs a climate of high temperature and moisture. It needs a temperature of 21° to 26° Celsius and 100-150 cm annual rainfall. questions.subject: social
questions.text: Explain the struggle of Marthanda Varma against the Dutch.

answer.value: Raja Marthanda Varma of Travancore (ruled 1729–1758) stood against the foreigners who were greedy for pepper and rescued his principality from them. He expanded his kingdom, shifted his capital from Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram, and made Travancore the richest province with Cochin as a centre of the spice trade. Finally, on 15 August 1753 a treaty was signed by which the Dutch forces surrendered their power to the Travancore province.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: What are the uses of GPS technology?

answer.value: The main objective of the Global Positioning System (GPS) is to indicate the location of a stationary or moving object or person by pointing out the exact latitude, longitude and height above sea level, and so it is also called a ‘Path finder’. answer.value: Public finance means the finances of the government. It studies the way the government manages its income, expenditure and debts. questions.subject: social
questions.text: What are the functions of banks?

answer.value: Functions of banks: (1) accepting deposits from the public and others; (2) lending money to the public (loans) and other institutions; (3) transferring money from one place to another (remittances); (4) collecting money by cheques, drafts and bills; (5) discounting bills; (6) hiring safe deposit lockers; (7) conducting foreign exchange transactions; (8) keeping valuables in safe custody; and (9) issuing letters of credit and guarantee.

Lending money to the public and institutions (loans)
Collecting money by cheques, drafts and bills

questions.text: What are the characteristics of Entrepreneurs?

answer.value: An entrepreneur is a creative and innovative person who has the ability to create and build something and the knack of sensing an opportunity where others see chaos and confusion. questions.subject: social
questions.text: Analyse the objectives of Brahma Samaj.

answer.value: The Brahmo Samaj was in the forefront of the social and religious reformation in the 19th century. It attempted to bring in reforms in the traditions and customs of the Hindu religion: it opposed idol-worship and polytheism and encouraged monotheism, and it condemned the performance of yagas and rituals. By exposing Indians to western political thought through English education, it also enabled the development of nationalism among Indians.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: What were the economic causes for the First war of Indian independence?

answer.value: Economic causes of the First War of Independence: due to the industrial revolution in England, Indian handicrafts and cottage industries suffered heavily and craftsmen became unemployed — the textile and wool industries in particular became sick and people lost their jobs. The British imposed a heavy tax on the sale of Indian goods in England; under the zamindari system the landlords exploited the farmers; and the ‘Inam Commission’ took back the gifted (Inam) lands without documents, insulting the holders and creating financial problems, which led the farmers to revolt.

An ‘Inam Commission’ was appointed and all the gifted lands without documents (‘Inam lands’) were taken back.". The MQP prints no answer key; answer sourced from the textbook per review_policy_v1 §2-4.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Explain the fundamental principles of India's foreign policy.

answer.value: The principles of Indian foreign policy are: (1) opposition to colonialism; (2) opposition to imperialism; (3) opposition to racial discrimination (apartheid); (4) the policy of non-alignment — after 1945 India remained neutral and protected its interest without joining either the American or Russian bloc; and (5) priority for the progress of African and Asian countries, so that colonised countries come into the mainstream of development.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: What are the effects of cyclones?

answer.value: Effects of cyclones: cyclones are very destructive and sometimes totally change the life of the people of cyclone-hit areas; they cause large-scale deaths; ocean tides inundate the inland water-bodies and make them salty; crops get totally destroyed; transport links, electricity supply and the daily life of the people get affected badly; and cyclone-hit areas suffer from infectious diseases leading to huge casualties.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Analyse the role of Sangolli Rayanna in the freedom struggle of Kitturu.

answer.value: Sangolli Rayanna’s name has remained famous along with that of Rani Chennamma. Rayanna was a brave soldier who fought for the independence of Kittur and felt it was his duty to liberate his motherland. He fought against the British and was imprisoned along with the queen, and was later released. He continued the struggle against the British, and many oral histories keep his memory alive as a hero of the Kittur freedom struggle.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Analyse the role of Dayanand Saraswati in reforming Indian society.

answer.value: Arya Samaj was established by Dayananda Saraswati, who travelled throughout the country giving lectures against innumerable meaningless practices. He reinterpreted the Vedas and advocated caste and gender equality, encouraged widow marriage, and urged people to use swadeshi goods. He propounded his teachings in the book ‘Satyartha Prakasha’, and the ‘Purification Ritual’ was the main activity of the Arya Samaj, by which converts to other religions were brought back to Hinduism. The Samaj established schools and colleges in many places, and his principles of Swarajya and Swadharma (‘India should be for Indians’) inspired people to take part in the freedom movement.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: How is Black soil different from Red soil?

answer.value: Black soil (also called Regur or Black Cotton soil) is found in the Deccan Trap — Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, western Andhra Pradesh and north Karnataka; it is formed from the weathering of igneous rock, contains more clay, is fertile and capable of retaining water, is rich in lime and magnesium carbonates and is highly suitable for cotton and dry farming. Red soil covers the largest area of the peninsular plateau (from Kanyakumari in the south to Jhansi in the north, and from Gujarat’s Kutch to the Rajmahal hills); its major crops are ragi, tobacco and oil seeds, and where irrigation is available it grows paddy, sugarcane and cotton.

It is fertile and capable of retaining water. ... This soil is more of lime and magnesium carbonates. It is highly suitable for dry farming. ... Red Soil : Largest area of peninsular Plateau covered with red soil. ... The major crops growing in this type of soil are ragi, tobacco and oil seeds. Areas having irrigation facilities grow paddy, sugarcane, cotton etc.". The MQP prints no answer key; answer sourced from the textbook per review_policy_v1 §2-4.

questions.subject: social
questions.text: Industries in India are located only in a few areas. Why?

answer.value: Industries are located only in a few areas because their location is influenced by the availability of raw materials, energy resources, market, transport facility, availability of labour and port facility, and also by the availability of land at low cost, technology and government policies. questions.subject: social
questions.text: Explain the measures taken to eradicate gender discrimination in India.

answer.value: To eradicate discrimination against gender minorities, following the 2014 Supreme Court judgment, the central and state governments have taken several initiatives: giving opportunities to get education, to join government jobs and to contest in elections, and providing 1% reservation in government jobs.
